entry_window: 2026-07-01 -> 2026-07-26 (PubMed [EDAT]); harvested retrospectively on 2026-08-01. COMPLETE listing of every PM-relevant record in the window: 368 unique records screened, 166 PM-relevant by title, 2 rejected as water-phase, 164 retained.

PAPERS.title: Long-term performance evaluation and seasonal field calibration of a low-cost particulate matter sensor
PAPERS.precis: Applying the MLR calibration model improved accuracy, achieving acceptable performance for PM2.5 throughout the entire sampling period and for PM10 across the entire period and warm months, with R² values of 0.62-0.93 and normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) of 10.7-24.36%.

PAPERS.title: Evaluation of low-cost sensors for size-resolved indoor particle monitoring
PAPERS.precis: Strong PNC-correlations were observed for 0.3-0.5 μm particles and 0.5-1.0 μm (R2 ~ 0.72) but decreased substantially for > 1.0 μm particles (R2 < 0.36).

PAPERS.title: Development of a high-resolution PM2.5 model in Taiwan using integrated low-cost air quality sensors and satellite observations
PAPERS.precis: The model demonstrated excellent performance, with a 10-fold CV R2 (RMSE) of 0.98 (1.23 μg/m3).

PAPERS.title: Applying satellite-derived PM2.5 data to policy-relevant air quality metrics
PAPERS.n: 2 satellite products x 3 allocation methods, US counties
PAPERS.precis: This agreement is evaluated with respect to concentration values, rankings, and the definition of counties as "passing" or "failing" the ALA annual PM2.5 benchmark of 9.0 μg/m3 (the 2024 EPA National Ambient Air Quality Standard for annual PM2.5).

PAPERS.title: Comparison of policy-relevant air quality metrics calculated with sparse in situ monitoring and contiguous satellite-derived data
PAPERS.precis: Risk factors likely contributing to larger differences between CDVEs and CDVs within non-aligned counties include ≤2 monitors, low (<7 μg/m3) or high (>10 μg/m3) CDVs, low (<0.05%) or high (>0.1%) monitor coverage, large county size, wildfires, mountains, deserts, and low urbanization.

PAPERS.title: Comparison of black carbon measurements using filter-specific reference transmittance to lab blanks or averaged unloaded filters
PAPERS.precis: The performances of linear regression models between Method 1 and all other methods were moderate to strong (R2 range: 0.42-0.93) in the second, third, and fourth quartiles; however, the models in the first quartile (eBC range: 1.3-2.9 μg/m3) performed poorly (R2 = 0.25-0.26), with error approximately 25% of the mean.

PAPERS.title: Determinants of in-home personal exposure to black carbon: the MobiliSense sensor-based study
PAPERS.precis: Our study suggests that in-home pollution can be reduced by improving home features, such as heating systems, or by reducing the infiltration of outdoor air pollutants into indoor microenvironment either by using air filters or redesigning the ventilation system.

PAPERS.title: Integrating audiovisual data for short-term particulate matter concentration prediction on urban sidewalks
PAPERS.precis: LightGBM achieved the best performance, yielding R2 values of 0.64-0.65 for 10 s predictions and 0.80 for 1 min predictions under random cross-validation.

PAPERS.title: Spatial variability and pollutant-specific mitigation effects of an urban vegetated park observed with a high-density air quality sensor network
PAPERS.precis: These results suggest that the limited PM2.5 reduction observed in this study is partly attributable to the small spatial extent of the park, highlighting the importance of vegetation area, density, and continuity for effective PM2.5 exposure mitigation.

PAPERS.title: A spatiotemporal machine learning framework for high-resolution PM2.5 estimation using reconstructed satellite aerosol observations
PAPERS.precis: Multiple ML models are evaluated, and a multi-layer perceptron is identified as the best-performing estimator, achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.82 with substantially reduced prediction errors compared to models driven by raw satellite inputs.

PAPERS.title: Application of stationary IoT sensor networks to reduce exposure to particulate matter during local hotspot events in a megacity
PAPERS.n: S-Dot IoT network, Seoul fireworks event
PAPERS.precis: A new alert protocol is suggested to help reduce public exposure to pollutants, mitigate associated health risks, and encourage behavioral changes to improve air quality.

PAPERS.title: Sensitivity of ultrafine particle and black carbon simulations to model resolution and emission data in urban environments
PAPERS.precis: At 5 km resolution, HERMESv3 reduces the systematic underestimation of pollutant concentrations compared to EMEP.

PAPERS.title: Extrapolating personal exposure measurements to air pollution from outdoor sources into annual mean estimates
PAPERS.n: personal campaigns extrapolated to annual means
PAPERS.precis: We found that ambient measurements assigned by the nearest monitor approach were consistently higher than those estimated by the matched-scaled approach and higher than personal exposure to air pollution from outdoor sources for all pollutants, indicating potential bias in epidemiological associations, under specific conditions concerning variability and random error.

PAPERS.title: Industrial condensable particulate matter: a missing source in PM2.5 source apportionment driving winter pollution in China
PAPERS.precis: Based on receptor modeling, CPM contributes a median of 3.6% (95% CI: 0.9%-14.5%) to urban PM2.5 across all four seasons in 2023, in the industrialized cities examined (Shanghai, Xi'an, Hefei, Shijiazhuang).

PAPERS.title: Characterization of traffic-related particulate matter in an urban tunnel: source apportionment of exhaust and non-exhaust emissions
PAPERS.precis: Results indicated that the EF for PM2.5 and PM10 were significantly higher during the warm days (26 ± 7.7 for PM2.5, 40.4 ± 9.7 for PM10) than during the cold days (12.9 ± 1.3 for PM2.5 and 16 ± 1.14 for PM10).

PAPERS.title: Ascertaining household-level exposure to air pollution in people with schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders
PAPERS.precis: Area-level deprivation was associated with higher prevalence of schizophrenia/OPD, whereas no clear differences were observed by urbanicity or air pollution exposure.

PAPERS.title: Micro- and nano-plastics in the coronary circulation and air pollution exposure in ischaemic heart disease presentation
PAPERS.precis: STEMI patients showed higher levels of interleukin-6 and tumour necrosis factor-α (P≤.006) and were exposed to higher levels of PM2.5 (P≤.012).

PAPERS.title: Air quality and health implications of exposure to ultrafine particle pollution
PAPERS.n: 1 km global UFP field + cohort meta-analysis
PAPERS.precis: We estimate a mortality density of 35.7 (15.8-65.5) per 100,000 people annually in Europe, and 27.4 (12.9-47.4) per 100,000 in North America, the latter being close to the global mean.

PAPERS.title: Joint effects of heat and fine particulate matter on out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Japan
PAPERS.precis: Heat (relative risk, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.02-1.06]; 99th versus 80th percentile); and PM2.5 (relative risk, 1.02 per 10 μg/m3 [95% CI, 1.01-1.03]) were independently associated with increased OHCA risk.

PAPERS.title: Association of joint exposure to PM2.5 and extreme heat with cardiovascular disease: a population-based cohort study
PAPERS.precis: Each 1% of AREHD and AREHH increase reduced onset time by 0.446% (95% CI: 0.304-0.587) and 1.379% (95% CI: 1.043-1.714), stronger in the elderly, males, and sedentary individuals.

PAPERS.title: Sequential mediating roles of MMP-12 and DNA methylation in air pollution-induced atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
PAPERS.precis: The results indicated that an IQR increment of PM2.5, PM10, PM1, and their components (BC, NH₄⁺, NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻, OM) was significantly associated with elevated serum MMP-7 (percentage change: 3.8%-12.4%) and MMP-12 (7.7%-19.9%).

PAPERS.title: Prenatal air pollution exposure and autism spectrum disorder in the ECHO Consortium
PAPERS.precis: Higher O3 was associated with higher SRS scores at the median (β per IQR increment = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.05, 1.61) and highest quantile (β = 2.19, 95% CI: 0.06, 4.32) in the meta-analysis.

PAPERS.title: The role of gut microbiota in the association between air pollution and cognitive function in older adults
PAPERS.precis: Higher air pollution levels were associated with increased circulating levels of 2-oxoglutarate and l-glutamine (key metabolites in neurodegenerative progression), which were further linked to higher odds of concurrent mild cognitive impairment (OR: 1.39-1.56) and an increased 2-year risk of cognitive decline (OR: 1.26-1.37).

PAPERS.title: Long-term outdoor air pollution and incidence of Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis and motor neuron disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
PAPERS.precis: There was no clear evidence that PM2.5 (1.01; 0.77-1.32) or nitrogen dioxide (NO2, 0.98, 95% CI: 0.95-1.01) were associated with MS risk or PM2.5 with MND risk (1.07, 95% CI: 0.86-1.33).

PAPERS.title: Impacts of contemporaneous air pollution exposure on cognitive performance in Kenya
PAPERS.n: portable monitors at HCAP testing sites
PAPERS.precis: Higher PM2.5 exposure during testing is associated with lower cognitive performance, particularly in executive function, memory, and visuospatial tasks.

PAPERS.title: The evolving clinical landscape of PM2.5-attributable hemorrhagic stroke in China, 1990-2050
PAPERS.precis: Despite severe demographic headwinds, China achieved substantial reductions in PM2.5-attributable hemorrhagic stroke mortality.

PAPERS.title: Fine particulate matter exposure and long-term lung-function trajectory in adults with cystic fibrosis
PAPERS.precis: After covariate adjustment, we did not find evidence of an adverse association between PM2.5 and annual change in FEV1 z-score in the overall cohort [+0.002 per 3 µg/m3 change in PM2.5 (95% CI -0.001, 0.005)] or across birth cohorts.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to PM2.5 and ozone and the risk of acute respiratory infections: community-based prospective cohort
PAPERS.n: 3,617 Shanghai residents followed weekly for 1 y
PAPERS.precis: In the fully adjusted model using the 12-month exposure window, each IQR increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher risks of ARIs (hazard ratio [HR] 1.594, 95% CI 1.340-1.897), with stronger associations observed for ILI (HR 1.948, 95% CI 1.484-2.557).

PAPERS.title: Sex-specific associations between ambient air pollution exposure thresholds and lung function in middle-aged and older Canadians
PAPERS.precis: low NO2 exposure was associated with greater reductions in FEV1 among males (-5.00%; 95% CI: -7.16, -2.84) than among females (-1.99%; 95% CI: -2.79, -1.19), and significantly reduced FVC among males(-3.58%; 95% CI: -5.15, -2.00) but not among females (-1.64%; 95% CI: -3.39, 0.11).

PAPERS.title: The impact of improved air quality on low birth weight and health inequalities in Spain, 2010-2018
PAPERS.precis: Relative to tertiary education, secondary and primary education were associated with increased LBW odds [1.32 (95% CI: 1.30-1.35); 1.76 (95% CI: 1.71-1.82)].

PAPERS.title: Maternal ambient air pollution exposure and risk of stillbirth in Georgia, USA
PAPERS.precis: Particulate matter showed strong associations in the second trimester exposure window for all stillbirths (PM10: HR = 1.07; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04, 1.11; PM2.5: HR = 1.05; 95% CI = 1.01, 1.09).

PAPERS.title: Prenatal exposure to ambient air pollution and fetal growth trajectories in Wuhan, China
PAPERS.precis: Compared with the reference trajectory group, exposure to higher PM2.5 during weeks 1-16 was significantly associated with lower odds of being in the "fast growth group" for AC (OR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.55, 0.84) and EFW (OR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.56, 0.91).

PAPERS.title: Prenatal air pollution exposure and placental biomarkers of oxidative stress and ageing: the BiSC cohort
PAPERS.n: 499 participants, placental mtDNAcn and telomere length
PAPERS.precis: Increasing levels of NO2 and PM2.5 during the 1st and 3rd trimesters and across the entire pregnancy, as well as black carbon during the 3rd trimester, were significantly associated with an increase in placental mtDNAcn.

PAPERS.title: Cord-blood black carbon particle burden and a C19MC extracellular-vesicle miRNA signature enriched for neurodevelopmental pathways
PAPERS.precis: Five of the ten candidate miRNAs were associated with BC at BH-FDR ≤0.10: hsa-miR-25-3p and hsa-miR-433-3p (positive associations) and hsa-miR-518a-3p, hsa-miR-519a-3p/519b-3p, and hsa-miR-520g-3p/520h (negative associations).

PAPERS.title: PM2.5-dominant disruption of male reproductive hormone homeostasis: fine versus coarse particulate matter
PAPERS.precis: In the 0-360 day exposure window, each 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with a 0.0675 increase in log-transformed FSH (95% CI: 0.0231, 0.1120) and a 0.1136 decrease in log-transformed T (95% CI: -0.1604, -0.0667).

PAPERS.title: Ultrafine particulate matter emitted from ships drives inflammation and susceptibility to viral infection
PAPERS.n: size-fractionated port PM + airway epithelial models
PAPERS.precis: In cell models of airway and alveolar epithelium, this cruise ship-associated ultrafine PM was markedly more pro-inflammatory than PM from other sites, while simultaneously reducing expression of a range of genes associated with the innate antiviral response.

PAPERS.title: Liver-derived, circulating xanthine oxidoreductase drives vascular impairment associated with inhalation of ultrafine particulates
PAPERS.precis: Drinking water supplemented with the XOR inhibitor febuxostat or nitrite (NaNO2-) partially prevented nTiO2-induced impairment of vascular reactivity.

PAPERS.title: Exposure timing is a determinant of fine particulate matter pulmonary, vascular, and metabolic toxicity in male mice
PAPERS.n: C57BL/6 males, CAP 6 h/d x 30 d, two circadian phases
PAPERS.precis: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) air pollution is associated with an increased cardiometabolic disease risk.

PAPERS.title: Circular RNA circDNAJC5 regulates ultrafine particle-disrupted microglial lipid metabolism via sphingolipid signalling
PAPERS.precis: We identified circDNAJC5, a lipid metabolism-associated circRNA, as significantly downregulated during PM0.1-induced lipid metabolic disruption.

PAPERS.title: Future chronic and acute air pollution deaths in China under climate change and emission reduction
PAPERS.precis: Future climate warming and population aging may lead to increased health risks from air pollution, while emission reductions can help alleviate the associated risks.

PAPERS.title: Meteorologically driven changes in future global air quality: physical and monetized impacts
PAPERS.n: GCM + atmospheric chemistry + health impact models
PAPERS.precis: We also highlight striking regional differences in the sign of net pollutant impacts by 2100, with net pollution decreases in the Northern Hemisphere driven by reductions in nitrate aerosol, while increases in both ozone and organic aerosol at higher temperatures lead to net increases in pollutant impacts in the Southern Hemisphere.

PAPERS.title: Changes in respiratory and cardiovascular morbidity air pollution risk and attributable burden in New York City
PAPERS.precis: NO2-attributable burden was higher than PM2.5 burden for asthma and CVD outcomes.

PAPERS.title: Workplace exposures may mask wildfire smoke-related exposure inequities and mortality
PAPERS.precis: Despite experiencing less ambient exposure to wildfire PM2.5, counties with higher portions of non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic Americans experienced higher work-related exposures.

PAPERS.title: Global disease burden attributable to ambient air pollution: disparities, determinants, and implications
PAPERS.precis: Despite the decline in age-standardized rates, the absolute number of deaths attributable to ambient PM2.5 and O3 both increased, driven primarily by population aging, population growth, and increasing exposure levels, although reductions in baseline mortality rates partly offset these increases.

PAPERS.title: Should household air quality monitoring be considered in selected patients with asthma and COPD?
PAPERS.n: 205 adults with COPD, asthma or bronchiectasis; 2 months
PAPERS.precis: Tobacco smoking, either active or passive, was significantly associated with PM2.5 levels (p<0.001).

PAPERS.title: Wildfire smoke indoors: a review of infiltration risk factors and exposure mitigation strategies
PAPERS.n: review of infiltration and portable-air-cleaner studies
PAPERS.precis: Exposure to the particulate matter (PM2.5) component of wildfire smoke is associated with cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity and mortality.

PAPERS.title: Underground versus outdoor air in the Wieliczka Salt Mine health resort: particulate matter and selected gaseous pollutants
PAPERS.n: treatment chamber versus adjacent outdoor air
PAPERS.precis: The underground chamber was characterised by markedly lower concentrations of anthropogenic pollutants than the outdoor environment.

PAPERS.title: Proteomic signatures of ambient air pollution and risk of type 2 diabetes
PAPERS.precis: Higher proteomic signature scores of PM2.5, NO2, SO2, and benzene were also associated with an elevated risk of T2D, with HRs (95% CIs) of 1.05 (1.00, 1.09), 1.17 (1.12, 1.23), 1.11 (1.06, 1.16), and 1.11 (1.06, 1.16) for a per-standard-deviation increase, respectively.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to air pollution and chronic kidney disease incidence: the Danish Nurse Cohort
PAPERS.precis: We found positive associations of modest magnitude between long-term exposure to air pollutants and CKD, with hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) per interquartile range: 1.18 (0.93-1.50) per 2.86 µg/m3 for PM2.5, 1.14 (0.93-1.40) per 3.33 µg/m3 for PM10, 1.13 (0.99-1.28) per 8.09 µg/m3 for NO2, and 1.09 (1.00-1.20) per 0.34 µg/m3 for BC.

PAPERS.title: Ambient air pollution and risk of active tuberculosis: a population-based cohort study in Taiwan
PAPERS.precis: After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, cigarette smoking, alcohol use, education level, income, and tuberculosis history, the adjusted hazard ratio was 1.16 (95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.34) for every 10-μg/m3 increase in the PM2.5 level.

PAPERS.title: Traffic-related air pollution and the risk of invasive and borderline epithelial ovarian tumours
PAPERS.precis: For borderline tumours, the adjusted OR (95% CIs) per IQR of NO2 was 1.36 (0.99-1.87), while for invasive cancer was 0.98 (0.79-1.21).

PAPERS.title: Synergistic control of greenhouse gases and air pollutants in the Greater Bay Area, China: Regional, sectoral and supply chain pathways
PAPERS.precis: Regionally, these emissions originated mainly from resource-intensive provinces such as Shandong, Hebei, and Henan, while at the city level, flows from Foshan and Guangzhou to Hong Kong dominated, contributing 64 % of intercity embodied emissions.

PAPERS.title: Significant contributions of sea spray aerosol to vertical ClNO2 formation over coastal South China
PAPERS.precis: Moreover, SSA not only enhances ClNO2 production but also increases the mixing ratios of chlorine and hydroxyl radicals at higher altitudes the following day (∼400 m), significantly boosting AOC, with an increase in AOC of up to 10 %.

PAPERS.title: Global and local impacts of multi-dimensional urban form on PM2.5 concentrations: A case study of the downstream urban agglomeration in the Yangtze River Delta
PAPERS.precis: The regional annual average PM2.5 concentration shows a continuous downward trend (decreasing from 60.77 μg/m3 in 2014 to 29.52 μg/m3 in 2022), with reductions ranging from 29.55% to 40.61% across individual cities.

PAPERS.title: Air pollution risks to wheat and mustard in Delhi agricultural airshed during the winter cropping season (2022-2025)
PAPERS.precis: Potential yield-loss risks for rabi wheat in Bahadurgarh, Rohat and Sonipat could be up to 15, 14.25 and 11.4% while that of mustard could be potentially reduced by 12, 11.4 and 10.54%, respectively.

PAPERS.title: Global information-seeking behavior of air pollution and cardiovascular disease: insights from google trends analysis
PAPERS.precis: Technical AP indicators showed weak or negative zero-order associations with most CVD terms; however, sensitivity analysis controlling for pandemic-related confounding revealed complete directional reversal for PM₂.₅, with partial correlations becoming significantly positive, indicating that original negative associations were pandemic-driven artefacts.

PAPERS.title: Epigenetically Regulated NOX4/NRF2 Axis Mediates PM2.5-Induced Ferroptosis and Inflammatory Response in Membranous Nephropathy
PAPERS.precis: Notably, pretreatment with GKT137831 or ferrostatin-1 attenuated the PM2.5-mediated reduction in cell viability and prevented the activation of ferroptosis and pro-inflammatory phenotypes in PAN-stimulated MPC5 cells.

PAPERS.title: Combined Effects of Air Pollution and Drought Stress in Tomato Landraces
PAPERS.precis: 3 commercial varieties as well as 2 Hungarian landraces were selected, effects of the combined stressors were evaluated based on biomass reduction and biochemical end-points such as photosynthetic pigments concentrations and peroxidase (POD) activity.

PAPERS.title: Greenland Emissions Contribute to Black Carbon Aerosols in the Arctic Marine Boundary Layer
PAPERS.precis: rBC concentrations were highest in the Greenland coastal region (2.4 ng m-3), compared with the open ocean (1.7 ng m-3) and the marginal ice zone (0.6 ng m-3).

PAPERS.title: Integrated spatial analysis and Gaussian dispersion modelling of airborne particulate matter from rice processing mill hubs in rural Bangladesh and associated public health risks
PAPERS.precis: AirQ⁺ health risk analysis revealed that PM₂.₅ exposure contributed to 39.78% of ALRI-related mortality in children under five, while in adults (≥ 30 years), it accounted for 48.01% of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), 56.25% of Ischemic Heart Disease (IHD), and 65.05% of stroke deaths.

PAPERS.title: Non-destructive characterization of atmospheric particulate matter using SEM-EDS: Elemental mapping as a tool for chemical composition assessment
PAPERS.precis: Blank filter characterization revealed that fiberglass filters contained Na, Ba, and Zn (~ 6%), while quartz filters is cleaner.

PAPERS.title: Ultrafine particles - rethinking air pollution risk
From Size-Resolved PAC Emissions to Age-Specific Respiratory Deposition: Toxicity Potential of Particulate PACs from Residential Coal and Biomass Combustion
PAPERS.precis: Respiratory deposition modeling showed clear age dependence: under the same exposure scenario, children had ∼40% higher total respiratory deposition of particulate PACs than adults.

PAPERS.title: Wildfire Smoke and Human Health: A Global Perspective on Respiratory Risks and Emerging Interventions
Size-specific health effects of particulate matter components on cardiovascular mortality: a weekly time-series study in Tianjin, China
PAPERS.precis: Generalized linear models with a quasi-Poisson distribution were used to estimate the excess risk (ER) associated with an interquartile range increase in exposure, with further analyses by cardiovascular disease (CVD) subtype, sex, and age, and additional adjustment for ozone (O3) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2).

PAPERS.title: Association of air pollutant levels and blood pressure variability in patients with essential hypertension: a distributed lag analysis study
PAPERS.precis: For every 10-μg/m³ increase in PM10, the maximum lag effect on nDBPSD(night time diastolic blood pressure standard deviation) and nDBPCV(night time diastolic blood pressure coefficient of variation) was observed at lag 5, with increments of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.16, 0.99) and 1.00 (95% CI: 0.19, 1.8) respectively.

PAPERS.title: Short-term exposure to ambient air pollutants increases the mortality risk of chronic kidney disease: a time-stratified case-crossover study in Zhejiang Province
PAPERS.precis: Using multi-day moving average lags (calculated as the mean exposure from the current day up to the specified preceding day), the most prominent ERs were observed for PM2.5 at lag02 (ER: 15.16%, 95% CI: 12.69-17.68), SO2 at lag03 (ER: 8.80%, 95% CI: 5.95-11.72), O3 at lag01 (ER: 5.67%, 95% CI: 2.07-9.39), and ...

PAPERS.title: Developmental exposure to cigarette smoke particulate matter induces cross-generational DNA methylation changes in zebrafish
PAPERS.journal: Comp Biochem Physiol C Toxicol Pharmacol
PAPERS.precis: Embryos were exposed to TPM (0.1, 0.2, or 0.3 μg/mL equi-nicotine units) from 6 to 96 h post fertilization (hpf).

PAPERS.title: Size-dependent characterization of toxic aerosol emissions from ignition of cryogenically processed black mass from fully charged lithium-ion batteries
PAPERS.precis: Higher battery state of charge (SOC) produced substantially greater particulate emissions, while metallic contamination intensified ignition and further increased aerosol concentrations.

PAPERS.title: Residential Air Pollution, Inhalation Injury, and Burn Recovery: A Burn Model System Study
PAPERS.precis: These associations were attenuated after adjustment; though PM2.5 exposure was associated with inhalation injury, which was strongly associated with prolonged ventilation, tracheostomy, lower Global Health scores, and lower employment at follow-up.

PAPERS.title: Association of surrounding greenness with preterm birth and the potential mediating role of ambient air pollution
PAPERS.precis: Greenness exposure was associated with lower odds of PTB, and this association was partially mediated by reduced ambient PM2.5 and NO2 pollution.

PAPERS.title: Ambient air pollution and glaucoma among middle-aged and older adults in China: Evidence from the China health and retirement longitudinal study
PAPERS.precis: Ambient PM10 and PM2.5 concentrations in the Q2 and Q3 quartiles were associated with a higher prevalence of glaucoma in the study population.

PAPERS.title: The impact of air pollution on paediatric hospital admissions for acute lower respiratory infections (ALRI) in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, during Hajj events
PAPERS.precis: Exposure to NO2 was significantly associated with an increased risk of same-day ALRI admissions in children during the Hajj events (RR = 1.033; 95% CI: 1.003-1.063 per IQR rise) but not outside the Hajj events.

PAPERS.title: Integrated weighted geospatial analysis and spatiotemporal assessment of key criteria air pollutants for hotspot identification and air quality risk assessment
PAPERS.precis: Monsoon rains significantly reduced pollutant levels.

PAPERS.title: Ambient PM2.5 and respiratory tract disorder-related outpatient visits among healthcare workers: an ecological time-series study
PAPERS.precis: Among 12,458 healthcare workers, short-term increases in weekly ambient PM2.5 concentrations were associated with higher outpatient visit counts for overall RTDs (IRR 1.139, 95% CI 1.059-1.225), common cold (1.164, 1.082-1.252), allergic rhinitis (1.240, 1.126-1.365), sinusitis (1.168, 1.017-1.342), and asthma (1.429, 1.003-2.037).

PAPERS.title: Does diet modify the effects of air pollution on lung function? A large cross-sectional study
PAPERS.precis: Exposure to PM2.5 per 5 μg/m3 increment was associated with reduced FEV1 in the low of -14.4 mL(95%CI: -26.8, -2.2) but not in medium and high fruit intake groups (+2.9 mL(95%CI: -13.8,19.7) and +9.7 mL(95%CI: -4.1,23.6), respectively).

PAPERS.title: Associations of green space and air pollution with insulin resistance: Analysis of repeated-measurements health examination data
PAPERS.precis: Each standard deviation increase in NDVI was associated with a decrease in METS-IR (β = -0.030; 95% CI: -0.039 to -0.021).

PAPERS.title: Mechanically driven aerosol emissions from electric toothbrushing: An overlooked indoor source with exposure and infection risk implications
PAPERS.precis: Results showed that emissions were dominated by respirable fine particles, with over 85% below 2.5 μm, while ultrafine particle levels showed no clear increase relative to the pre-brushing baseline, indicating a distinct emission regime compared to respiratory processes.

PAPERS.title: Semi-parametric methods for long-term trend detection in air quality: The North-Eastern Italian Alps case
PAPERS.precis: Model performance varied by pollutant, with higher accuracy for gases (R2 up to 0.86 for O3) than for particulate matter (R2 of approximately 0.66).

PAPERS.title: Near-road particulate matter from Washington D.C. has variable levels of 6PPD and 6PPD-quinone: acute and developmental impacts in zebrafish
PAPERS.precis: NR1 and NR2 elicited similar increases in other morphological abnormalities, although responsiveness to changes in light after developmental exposure was diminished to a greater extent with NR2 compared to NR1.

PAPERS.title: Nanoparticle-Encapsulated 5-Azacytidine Attenuates Air Pollution-Induced Human Cardiac Fibroblast Activation
PAPERS.precis: HCFs were exposed to PM0.49 (low and high concentrations), with or without pre-treatment using free 5-Aza or 5-Aza-loaded hyaluronic acid nanoparticles (5-Aza-NP).

PAPERS.title: Respiratory health outcomes following co-exposure to subchronic high temperature, episodic wildfire smoke exposure, and high-cholesterol diet
PAPERS.precis: To determine effects of ongoing exposure, 4-5-week-old rats were subchronically housed at RT or high temperature (HT; 30-31°C) and fed ND or high-cholesterol (2%) diet (HCD).

PAPERS.title: Prenatal Air Pollution Exposure and Child Lungs: Innovations in Measurement and Causal Inference
Identifying sources of black carbon associated with high mortality risk in Beijing, China based on long-term hourly continuous measurements
PAPERS.precis: The findings indicated that the health risk of BC could vary by source, with traffic BC posing the highest non-accidental mortality risk (RR: 1.014, 95% CI: 1.003, 1.025), followed by biomass burning and atmospherically aged BC.

PAPERS.title: Spatial clustering of air pollutant trends and exposure burden across Romania (2013-2024)
PAPERS.precis: The Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope estimator, and Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) are used to quantify trends and detect spatially coherent clusters.

PAPERS.title: Ambient PM2.5 exposure is associated with clear cell renal cell carcinoma aggressiveness and promotes tumor progression through ROS-mediated AKT/HIF-2α signaling
